name: Acid-Washed Knit Beanie (Rolled Cuff)
description: A ribbed knit beanie in dark teal gone patchy and pale from repeated exposure to Shelf acid-rain, the color now a mottled map of where the rain hit hardest. Rolled cuff is double-thick for ear coverage in lake-effect wind. A small repair darn sits near the crown where the knit snagged on something and tore through.
functionality: Double-rolled cuff covers ears in sub-zero wind; snug fit stays on in a lake-effect gust.
what_it_says: This person has been out in Shelf weather long enough to wear it into their clothing — the acid-bleach is a record of time spent outside.
worn_by: anyone braving a Meridian winter without a hood
manufacturer: Unknown — knit goods, Shelf handmade market
story_hooks: The acid-rain pattern on this particular beanie matches a specific block's micro-weather — someone who knows the Shelf could tell you exactly where this person spends their time.
A tiny knot of a different-colored yarn is worked into the darn near the crown — a maker's mark, a memorial stitch, or just what was available.
